title: File trademark
summary: File a trademark application with the USPTO for the company name and/or logo.

parts.title: Conduct trademark search
parts.guidance: Define the mark, goods or services and territories, then search for identical and similar wording or designs using the relevant trademark-office tools. Capture potentially relevant marks, owners, status and goods or services, along with the search terms. Send the clearance questions to the legal reviewer. An available domain or empty exact-name search does not clear the mark.

parts.title: Determine filing classes
parts.guidance: Describe what customers buy under the mark and any concrete planned offerings. Map these to the selected office’s classification tools and proposed wording. Review uncertain classes and the resulting fees and coverage with the filing adviser. Specify the goods and services for which protection is sought.

parts.title: Draft goods/services description
parts.guidance: Draft the identification using the actual offering and the office’s accepted terminology. Match it to the intended filing basis and flag uncertain scope or classifications for the adviser. Check product facts with the people who know the service and retain relevant use evidence or development plans. Avoid claiming unrelated products merely to broaden the wording.

parts.title: Review with IP attorney
parts.guidance: Review the search results, owner, mark representation, territories, goods/services wording and filing-basis evidence with trademark counsel. Resolve clearance risks, ownership questions, representation requirements and the filing strategy. The applicant can then decide whether to proceed with the identified risks and costs. Registration remains subject to the office’s examination and any further proceedings.

cost.note: Attorney fees vary — no published sticker price exists.

parts.title: File application on USPTO.gov
parts.guidance: Use the office selected in the filing strategy. For the US, prepare the approved owner, mark, goods/services, filing basis and evidence in the current USPTO service. The applicant or authorized representative reviews the declarations, signs and authorizes submission and payment. Keep the filed application, receipt and serial number for monitoring. A foreign option uses that office’s procedure.

options.title: Default — USPTO trademark application
options.summary: Submit the reviewed US owner, mark, filing basis, goods/services and evidence through the current USPTO filing service. The applicant or authorized representative must approve the declarations, signature and fees. Save the filed copy and serial number and monitor official correspondence. The receipt records submission; the examination and any further requirements continue afterward.

verify.how: TSDR shows the application's serial number and status — newly filed applications appear within a few days.

cost.note: USPTO base application fee, per class of goods/services (fee code 7017); surcharges apply for custom identifications or insufficient information.

options.title: India - CGPDTM e-filing
options.summary: Use the approved Indian owner, mark representation, goods/services and supporting evidence in the current IP India filing route. Confirm account and signature requirements from the official instructions. The authorized filer approves the application and fee, then retains the acknowledgement and application number. Monitor the Indian matter through IP India correspondence and status tools.

options.title: UK - UK IPO filing
options.summary: Prepare the intended owner, mark and goods/services for the UK IPO route. Review classes, the current fee and any special application choice before the authorized applicant submits. Keep the acknowledgement and monitor official communications. Record the territory sought and establish a separate filing strategy for requested protection outside the UK.
options.when: Filing the mark in the United Kingdom

references.title: UK IPO - register a trade mark

options.title: Germany - DPMA (or EUIPO) filing
options.summary: Confirm whether the strategy calls for a German national mark or a separate EU route. For the national application, use DPMA’s current service with the reviewed owner, representation and goods/services. The authorized filer approves declarations and fees before submission. Track the DPMA reference number; any EU application remains a separate matter with its own advice and filing evidence.

options.title: France - INPI (or EUIPO) filing
options.summary: Prepare the applicant, mark and goods/services in INPI’s trademark portal. Review the complete summary and coverage before the authorized filer validates and pays, then retain the acknowledgement and national filing number. Monitor INPI correspondence for the matter. Broader EU protection needs a separate strategy; this trademark filing is also distinct from INPI company-formation formalities.

parts.title: Track application status
parts.guidance: Monitor the official status and correspondence for the application number. Record response deadlines and send substantive office actions or oppositions to counsel promptly. Keep the office’s contact information current and preserve responses and filing receipts. When registration or another disposition occurs, hand any maintenance or further action to its responsible person.

metadata.supportReason: USPTO has no usable API. System provides guidance, drafts descriptions, and tracks deadlines, but filing is manual.

geoNotes.summary: Trade marks are filed with the Controller General (CGPDTM) through the IP India e-filing portal; public search runs on the separate tmrsearch portal.
UK marks are filed online with the UK IPO (from £170); since Brexit an EUIPO registration no longer covers the UK, so UK + EU protection means two filings.
geoNotes.actionLabel: UK IPO — register a trade mark

geoNotes.summary: National marks are filed with the DPMA (DPMAdirekt online filing); the EU-wide alternative is a single EUIPO application covering all 27 member states.
French marks are filed online with the INPI; as in Germany, an EUIPO application is the single-filing route to EU-wide protection.

National marks are filed online with INPI (Instituto Nacional da Propriedade Industrial); the EU-wide alternative is a single EUIPO application covering all 27 member states, so PT + EU protection is usually one EUIPO filing.
File with CIPO (online, Nice-classified, with Madrid Protocol available for international extension) — and budget for the queue: CIPO examination waits run years, so file early.
